headlines: 10-year Treasury yield hits highest level since 2002 as global bond rout gathers pace
Oil prices rise as Chinese refiners reportedly ban October fuel exports; Brent crude back above $100
US Futures Mixed as Micron Outlook and Nike Results Take Focus: Dow Jones, S&P, Nasdaq, Wall Street
Calls for gas tax suspensions grow as Americans struggle with high prices
Supreme Court Weighs Shield for Oil Companies as New Term Opens
Teen's tragic killing by illegal immigrant becomes flashpoint in battle for control of Congress

cards.hearing: You may be hearing about oil prices and calls to pause gas taxes, as households feel pressure at the pump.
cards.why: Fuel matters beyond the cost of filling a car: trucks use it to move groceries and other everyday goods.
cards.but: But a fuel headline is one piece of the picture, not a reason to abandon a long-term investment plan.
cards.story: Picture planning a long drive and running into a detour. You adjust the route, but you don't cancel the trip; a good plan can stay on course through a noisy stretch.
say: We can notice the fuel story without letting it rewrite your long-term plan.

cards.hearing: Stocks slipped a little yesterday, while interest rates ticked higher. The facts point to a quieter market week, not a major event today.
cards.why: Higher interest rates can make borrowing more expensive for households and businesses, including when they finance a home or a project.
cards.but: But a small move in stocks and a shift in rates are reasons to stay informed, not to lose sight of the long-term plan.
cards.story: Imagine a garden with several kinds of plants. One may have a rough week while another is doing fine; variety helps keep one patch from defining the whole garden.
say: We built your plan for a mix of conditions, not just one market day.

cards.hearing: You may hear that long-term borrowing costs are climbing around the world, and the rate on U.S. government bonds has reached its highest level in more than two decades.
cards.why: That matters because long-term rates can affect the cost of mortgages and other loans, which may shape a household’s budget.
cards.but: But a change in rates is one part of the financial picture, not a reason to abandon a long-term plan.
cards.story: Imagine planning a long road trip and finding one stretch of traffic. You adjust your pace, but you don’t forget where you’re headed.
say: Rates are worth watching, but we’ll keep your long-term plan in view.
We can take this week as it comes without letting one headline steer the whole journey.
